identification: Pair of spindle-back kitchen chairs with shaped saddle seats and ring-turned legs and stretchers. Photos show a common Victorian-style 'cottage/kitchen' pattern (seat looks like elm, not clearly blackwood), with no jawbone supports. Known George Peddle chairs sold at Leski have jawbone supports; these do not show that feature. Peddle attribution is unverified and looks weak.

viewing_check: Look under the seats and on the back of the top rail and rear legs for a stamp, label or branded 'PEDDLE' mark. Check whether the timber is blackwood or elm/beech, whether any jawbone-style supports exist, and joint tightness and splits in the saddle seats. Without a mark or jawbone, treat as ordinary kitchen chairs.
